_about: Public procurement publishers that expose awards in the Open Contracting Data Standard (OCDS) release or record format, so an award to a supplier can be stored as a FundsTransfer with the buyer as the funding party. One generic parser reads them all because the data schema is standard; what differs per publisher is the query API, described here as data. query_url is a template with {supplier} (URL-encoded supplier name) and optional {page}; a publisher is used only when enabled is true and query_url supports searching by supplier. Many OCDS publishers offer only bulk or date/ID paging, not supplier search, and some large economies (e.g. China) publish no open procurement data at all; those stay disabled until a usable supplier-search endpoint is confirmed. enabled is set true only after the query_url and the response envelope are validated against a real sample from that publisher (see the TED validation approach). Each entry cites the publisher's own documentation (ai-design-principles.md, principle 11). name is the canonical Organization name stored for the publisher's platform; country is the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code.

publishers.name: Portal Nacional de Contratações Públicas
publishers.note: Brazil's national portal (PNCP) has an API but publishes its own schema, not OCDS releases; needs either an OCDS export endpoint or a dedicated parser.

publishers.name: Contrataciones Abiertas (México)
publishers.note: Mexico publishes OCDS through many federal and sub-national bodies (OCP data registry); confirm a publisher that supports supplier search before enabling.

publishers.name: Open Contracting India (CivicDataLab)
publishers.note: India's OCDS data is state-level (e.g. Himachal Pradesh, Assam) via CivicDataLab, largely bulk; confirm a supplier-searchable endpoint before enabling.
